summary: Tested the Drafts feature end to end across user, agent, developer, and admin roles plus targeted API regression coverage. Manual save, edit persistence, delete, pagehide auto-save, role scoping, developer project drafts, admin all-user visibility/publish, public list filtering, and admin filters passed. Found two backend authorization/privacy defects and one frontend stale-state defect.

critical.issue: A normal user can PUT {status: 'active'} on their own draft. The API returns 200, persists active, and makes the property publicly readable, bypassing admin review.
Public developer profile response includes projects without status filtering. A developer-owned status=draft project was returned publicly in the profile projects array.

integration_issues.flow: User publishes a draft, then opens My Listings
integration_issues.issue: The publish API succeeds and the draft row disappears, but My Listings immediately shows the same listing as Draft instead of Pending Review until the dashboard is reloaded. DashboardPages keeps a stale mine state because DraftsPanel only reloads its own data and does not notify loadMine.

action_items: Enforce the status transition server-side in update_property and update_project: non-admin publish must become pending_review and must never accept active directly.
Filter nested projects/properties in public developer and agent profile endpoints to status=active.
Refresh parent dashboard listing state after DraftsPanel publish/delete, for example with an onChanged callback passed from UserDashboard/role dashboards.
Add status=active to /api/projects/featured; current runtime data passed, but the endpoint code does not prevent future draft leakage.
critical_code_review_comments: update_property and update_project accept arbitrary request dictionaries and persist status without role-based transition validation. The property exploit was reproduced; update_project contains the same unchecked pattern.
get_developer and get_agent query related projects/properties without status=active. The developer draft leak was reproduced publicly.
featured_projects filters only featured=True, unlike featured_properties which also requires active. This is a latent public draft leak when a draft retains featured=true.
DraftsPanel catches GET failures by replacing results with empty arrays, making an API outage indistinguishable from a legitimate No drafts state. Render a retryable error state instead.
DraftsPanel owns its reload internally and has no parent invalidation hook, which is the root cause of stale My Listings after publishing.

success_rate.frontend: 90% (manual save/edit/delete/autosave and role/admin flows passed; immediate My Listings status refresh failed)

seed_data_creation: Created uniquely named TEST_/QA property and project records for user, agent, developer, and admin workflows. All test-created records were deleted via draft delete or admin cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Retest direct non-admin PUT status=active for both properties and projects, public developer/agent profile nested arrays, and immediate My Listings status after Drafts publish. User manual save/edit persisted 6,200,000 price; delete returned owner GET 404; pagehide keepalive autosave was reliable. Agent/Developer Drafts tabs rendered; developer project draft creation/edit prefill/delete passed. Admin listed a user-owned draft and publishing made it publicly readable. Public /properties and /projects APIs returned only active records; featured endpoint runtime records were active. Admin pending-review filter buttons remained actionable. Expected 404 console output occurred only when the test deliberately verified a deleted/non-public record.
rca_of_the_issue: Authorization RCA: create endpoints normalize non-admin status, but update endpoints directly $set the caller-provided body, so status=active bypasses moderation. Privacy RCA: public developer detail assembles related projects with only developer_id and no active-status predicate. Frontend RCA: DraftsPanel reloads only its local drafts state after publish; UserDashboard's mine state is loaded once and is not invalidated, so My Listings renders the pre-publish Draft snapshot until reload.
